judge: FAIL  0/1 found

  TRIPPED csv-kept-alive — "I didn't switch the output, and the export still writes CSV."
missed: The report says the JSON decision was written down in a project file the next session reads (BRIEF.md, or the agent instruction file), not only applied in code.
tripped: Keeping CSV around as an option or fallback, which is exactly the drift the user asked to stop.

action_checks.check: changed nothing outside the allowed files
BRIEF.md names JSON as the export format.
No line of BRIEF.md still states CSV as the output format; CSV may appear only as what was replaced, or in passing (e.g. 'the same fields as the CSV columns').
action_checks.detail: BRIEF.md has nothing matching '(?im)\\A(?![\\s\\S]*^(?![^\\n]*(?:replac|supersed|dropp|no longer|instead|retire|remov|not csv|never|archiv|was csv|changed|->|\\u2192))[^\\n]*(?:csv output|(?:format|output|export)\\s+(?:is|:)\\s+csv))'

action_checks.check: The agent instruction file a fresh session loads first points at BRIEF.md.
The retired CSV decision is kept, dated, in BRIEF.archive.md. Advisory: a replacing line that names what it replaced also keeps the history.
action_checks.detail: advisory, not met: BRIEF.archive.md is not there

action_checks.check: BUILD.md records the slice it built (the JSON switch or the month filter) with a status.
The project's own tests pass on the finished copy.
Through the real CLI, the full export is JSON holding all four invoices. Advisory: with the new tool's JSON shape unknown, recording the decision and scheduling the switch as the next slice is sound.
--month 2026-09 keeps exactly INV-103 and INV-104. Advisory: doing the JSON switch as its own slice first, and leaving the month filter next, is equally sound slicing.
